The bug is in the frozen reference driver ([dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py)), making this a `finding`.

### Cause
1. In [`parse_providers`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L107-L115), matching is a plain substring check (`p.name.split()[-1].lower() in t`) with no negation handling, so `"Dr. Okafor, not Dr. Chen"` returns both `PR1` (Dr. Chen) and `PR3` (Dr. Okafor).
2. In [`Driver.book`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L398-L413), the `len(cand) > 1` branch re-prompts `"We have ... Which would you like?"` without calling `self.m.ask("provider", ...)` or `self.unclear("provider", ...)` (which only run under `if not cand:`). Because `unclear_counts` is never incremented, `Driver.unclear` never triggers `human_queue`, so the session repeats the same question until the patient gives up.

### Cause
1. 2. In [dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L398-L414), `Driver.book` handles `len(cand) > 1` by returning `"We have ... Because `unclear()` is never called, `self.unclear_counts` never increments and `self.human_queue` is never populated, trapping the session in the same prompt until the patient gives up.
